rule.title: A noncash gift over $5,000 needs a qualified appraisal

when_missing.because: Taken as no unless a preparer says so: Is this a noncash gift (or group of similar items) claimed at over $5,000 with no qualified written appraisal, and none of the exceptions applies (a qualified vehicle with a written acknowledgment, certain inventory, publicly traded securities, certain intellectual property)?

citation.wording: If you claim a deduction of over $5,000 for a noncash charitable contribution, you must have the contemporaneous written acknowledgement (see CWA, earlier), obtain a qualified written appraisal of the donated property from a qualified appraiser, and complete Form 8283, Section B.
